All fields submitted. Here's the final tie-out to RAP-04:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **flagged_contracts** | CTR-2047, CTR-2052, CTR-2055, CTR-2058 |
| **amount_exceptions** | CTR-2047, CTR-2052 |
| **timing_exceptions** | CTR-2055, CTR-2058 |
| **over_recognised_usd** | $7,500 (CTR-2052: $157,500 recognised vs $150,000 contract) |
| **under_recognised_usd** | $8,000 (CTR-2047: $88,000 recognised vs $96,000 contract) |

---

**What the auditors will see:**

- **CTR-2052 (Alder & Roe)** — 12 × $13,125 = $157,500 against a $150,000 contract. The schedule was built on the wrong monthly amount; $7,500 over-recognised is a restatement risk.

- **CTR-2047 (Cedar Line Media)** — Nov/Dec drop from $8,000 to $4,000, leaving $8,000 on the table. That's a cut-off risk.

- **CTR-2055 (Bellhaven)** — 13 periods on a 12-month contract (trails into April 2026). Total ties to the cent but one extra month is still a recognition error.

- **CTR-2058 (Quill River)** — 8 periods on a 12-month contract; $108,000 crammed into 8 months instead of 12. Total ties but the acceleration is a timing exception same as Bellhaven.

The register's linked column (stale from Jan 15) matches the schedule in every case — the problems are in the schedules themselves, which is exactly what the auditors found last year.
